rationale.String: Pre-validation preserves rejected-command byte identity and makes the transaction auditable.

rejected_alternatives.String: ["deduct currency before validating the current level","partially apply the effect on an insufficient-balance rejection","silently clamp purchases at maximum level"]

replacement_condition.String: Released transaction logic or reproducible observations close every rejection branch and event order.

selected_policy.String: Validate current level and balance before deducting currency; commit cost, level and effect as one ordered operation.

unavailable_fact.String: The exact rejection event ordering for insufficient balance, wrong current level and maximum level is not published.

rationale.String: one-attempt exclusion makes refresh meaningful while the bounded fallback prevents an artificial dead end

rejected_alternatives.String: ["allow the identical offer without an explicit fallback","permanently exclude every previously seen candidate for the battle"]

replacement_condition.String: replace when released logic or reproducible observations define refresh exclusion memory and fallback

selected_policy.String: exclude the immediately displayed candidate IDs for one refresh attempt, then fall back to the full legal pool if exclusion would empty it

unavailable_fact.String: released sources do not fully specify whether every just-rejected candidate remains eligible after refresh

rationale.String: draw ordinal preserves causality and stable ID removes locale/platform dependence

rejected_alternatives.String: ["sort by localized display name","preserve filesystem or hash-map iteration order"]

replacement_condition.String: replace when released data exposes an explicit offer ordinal or a reproducible observation proves a different order

selected_policy.String: preserve labeled draw ordinal; break duplicate/tie positions by stable ID ascending

unavailable_fact.String: the stable order of simultaneously drawn choices is not fully published

rationale.String: Entry-position sampling preserves all source information while making the hidden distribution explicitly replaceable.

rejected_alternatives.String: ["deduplicate repeated stable IDs before sampling","treat authored array order as descending hidden weight","use generic shuffle or collection iteration order"]

replacement_condition.String: Released logic defines treasure group timing, weights, count and duplicate handling.

selected_policy.String: Use labeled project integer sampling over eligible authored entry ordinals; repeated positions remain distinct and stable.

unavailable_fact.String: The released tables expose ordered entry lists but not selection weights, group timing or duplicate-entry semantics.

rationale.String: stable combatant identity preserves deterministic replay without changing target eligibility

rejected_alternatives.String: ["use battlefield insertion order without an authored contract","use a floating random shuffle"]

replacement_condition.String: replace when released target-order data or reproducible observations prove a different selector

selected_policy.String: sort eligible targets by the project stable combatant key before labeled integer selection or first-target choice

unavailable_fact.String: several weapon target selectors do not publish tie-breaking among equally eligible combatants

rationale.String: uniform stable-ID sampling is deterministic, neutral and does not manufacture hidden rarity weights

rejected_alternatives.String: ["infer weights from rarity or display position","reuse upstream table iteration order as a probability distribution"]

replacement_condition.String: replace when released structured weights or a reproducible released-version observation establishes the complete distribution

selected_policy.String: sample uniformly by project integer sampling from eligible stable IDs sorted lexicographically

unavailable_fact.String: released sources do not expose a complete authoritative draw weight for every eligible offer

rationale.String: phase/priority preserves known timing while stable ID is replay-safe

rejected_alternatives.String: ["order by acquisition time","order by localized weapon name"]

replacement_condition.String: replace when released structured priority data or reproducible observations establish a different tie-break

selected_policy.String: order ready weapon triggers by trigger phase, authored priority when present, then stable weapon ID

unavailable_fact.String: same-boundary ordering between multiple ready weapons is not fully described in released text

rationale.String: tier and stable-ID order is bounded, auditable and keeps recipe consumption atomic

rejected_alternatives.String: ["always apply duplicate upgrade before synthesis","choose an eligible recipe using an unlabeled random draw"]

replacement_condition.String: replace when released program evidence or a reproducible observation proves the exact simultaneous resolution order

selected_policy.String: evaluate explicit synthesis candidates first by tier then recipe stable ID; otherwise apply the ordinary duplicate upgrade

unavailable_fact.String: the order between a newly eligible synthesis and an ordinary duplicate upgrade in one offer is not public for every recipe tier

rationale.String: named contribution boundaries minimize invented rounding while producing deterministic integer totals

rejected_alternatives.String: ["round after every multiplication","banker's-round only the final aggregate"]

replacement_condition.String: replace when released formula programs or exact observations identify the authoritative rounding boundary and mode

selected_policy.String: retain canonical fixed-point intermediates and round toward zero only at each explicitly authored integer score contribution boundary

unavailable_fact.String: released score displays do not expose every intermediate rounding boundary

rationale.String: bounded explicit failure preserves state and avoids nontermination

rejected_alternatives.String: ["retry an unbounded random draw","silently replace or downgrade an owned maximum-level item"]

replacement_condition.String: replace when released structured logic or reproducible observation defines each empty-candidate branch

selected_policy.String: emit a ReferenceOnly no-candidate outcome, consume no inventory resource and continue at the next declared lifecycle boundary

unavailable_fact.String: released text does not define every empty-pool/full-inventory combination

rationale.String: Ordinal retention is lossless and avoids inventing a mapping not present in released structured facts.

rejected_alternatives.String: ["name the ordinals small, medium and large from array position","convert the decimals into host floating probability draws","reorder the vector by value"]

replacement_condition.String: Released logic binds every ordinal to a named chest state and sampling boundary.

selected_policy.String: Retain both vectors by ordinal and do not assign chest-tier names or floating draws.

unavailable_fact.String: The semantic names and application timing of the three probability ordinals are not exposed by the constant table.

rationale.String: The ranks are requested progression facts, but public community evidence must remain visibly lower-quality than structured rows.

rejected_alternatives.String: ["infer rank costs from Departure values","derive costs from the value of account rewards","drop reputation ranks because their reward payload is excluded"]

replacement_condition.String: A pinned released structured Offering definition provides every Demon King rank cost.

selected_policy.String: Retain the pinned public revision's 3000x5, 4500x5 and 6000x10 costs as ReferenceOnly cross-check data; import no reward payload.

unavailable_fact.String: A released structured Offering table for all 20 Demon King rank costs is absent from the frozen structured family.
